title: Set up company email & docs
summary: Configure the company email, calendar, and docs suite for the team, including admin settings. Google Workspace is the canonical route.

parts.title: Create the company email workspace
parts.guidance: Compare the selected email and document platform with the team's required applications, domain, user count, and existing accounts. Decide who will administer the tenant, manage billing, and recover access if an administrator leaves. Get the budget owner's approval for the subscription, then create or reuse the company workspace. Keep domain verification, mailbox provisioning, and switching incoming mail as separate setup tasks, with an owner for the cutover.

options.title: Default — Google Workspace signup
options.summary: Use this path when Google Workspace is the chosen platform. Check whether the company domain already belongs to a tenant, then use a company-controlled administrator account to start the selected subscription within the agreed budget. Google's setup flow will provide the current domain-verification and mail-activation instructions. Prepare users and destination mailboxes before changing incoming mail routing, and keep the administration link and recovery arrangements available to the company's IT owner.

references.title: Google Workspace: Verify a domain and activate Gmail

options.title: Microsoft 365 workspace
options.summary: Use this path for a Microsoft 365 workspace. Match the subscription to the required applications and user licenses, and check for an existing tenant before creating one. Establish company-controlled administration and the agreed billing arrangement. Follow Microsoft's current domain-connection instructions, provision the people who receive company email, and plan migration of existing mail and files. Keep the mail-routing change separate until the destination mailboxes and the people using them are ready.
options.when: The team and its buyers live on Outlook/Teams

parts.title: Verify domain ownership
parts.guidance: Get the verification value from the workspace's current setup flow and identify the administrator of the company's DNS zone. Add the exact requested record through that administrator, preserving unrelated records, then ask the provider to verify it. If verification fails, compare the saved name and value with the provider's instructions and check public DNS resolution. Successful domain verification establishes control of the domain; incoming email still follows its configured mail-routing records.

references.title: Google Workspace: Verify a domain and activate Gmail

parts.title: Create user accounts
parts.guidance: Create individual accounts from the team roster using consistent company addresses and the licenses each role needs. Resolve address collisions and use the platform's appropriate shared-address setup for functions such as billing or support. Give each person their sign-in and recovery instructions through the normal onboarding channel. Confirm that the mailboxes needed for cutover exist and identify any user whose old mail, contacts, or files still need migration.

parts.title: Set up shared drives
parts.guidance: Create shared drives or libraries around who owns the documents and who needs access. Separate general team material from finance, personnel, legal, and other restricted records. Check how the selected platform handles shared ownership and departing users, then assign responsible groups and maintainers. Place a few real documents in their intended locations and check access with a reader and an editor. Publish a short filing guide so new documents land in the right place.

parts.title: Configure security settings
parts.guidance: Review administrator roles, sign-in protection, recovery methods, and external-sharing settings with the IT owner. Prioritize administrator and sensitive-mailbox access, and establish a recovery path before enforcing settings that could lock people out. Roll changes out to a small group first, checking normal sign-in and the sharing workflows the team relies on. Resolve exceptions, then extend the settings and document who manages recovery, suspicious activity, and future access changes.

metadata.supportReason: Google Admin API supports user/group management. Initial domain setup and billing are manual.
